extraction.name: Natural Questions: A Benchmark for Question Answering Research
extraction.description: The Natural Questions corpus, a question answering data set consisting of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine paired with Wikipedia pages. Annotators provide long answers (typically a paragraph) and short answers (one or more entities) if present on the page.
extraction.creator: Tom Kwiatkowski, Jennimaria Palomaki, Olivia Redfield, Michael Collins, Ankur Parikh, Chris Alberti, Danielle Epstein, Illia Polosukhin, Jacob Devlin, Kenton Lee, Kristina Toutanova, Llion Jones, Matthew Kelcey, Ming-Wei Chang, Andrew M. Dai, Jakob Uszkoreit, Quoc Le, Slav Petrov
extraction.citeAs: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics, vol. 7, pp. 453–466, 2019.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions consist of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine. Simple heuristics are used to filter questions from the query stream. The questions are paired with Wikipedia pages from the top 5 search results.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine and Wikipedia pages from the top 5 search results.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Simple heuristics are used to filter questions from the query stream. Questions are sampled that either start with 'who', 'when', or 'where' followed by specific verb forms, contain multiple entities with modifiers, or end with categorical noun phrases.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions of 8 words or more issued by multiple users in a short period of time were selected. Heuristics were applied to discard non-questions. Only queries where a Wikipedia page appeared in the top 5 search results were kept.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: An annotator is presented with a question along with a Wikipedia page. The annotator selects an HTML bounding box (long answer) containing the information required to answer the question, or marks null if no answer is present. If a long answer is present, the annotator selects a short answer (entity span, boolean yes/no, or null). Annotation is performed using a custom annotation interface by a pool of around 50 annotators.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper discusses human variability and ambiguity in annotations. It presents analysis of 25-way annotations on 302 examples to understand disagreement. It also performs post-hoc evaluation using four experts to determine precision (90% for long answers, 84% for short answers) and categorizes answers as Correct, Correct (but debatable), or Wrong.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Single annotations for training data; 5-way annotations for development and test data; 25-way annotations for a subset of 302 examples.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: A pool of around 50 annotators. Four experts (the first four authors of the paper) were used for post-hoc evaluation.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Google’s Cloud NLP API (used for identifying part-of-speech tags and entities during heuristic filtering).
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The queries are anonymized and aggregated.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is designed to drive research in natural language understanding and provide large-scale end-to-end training data for question answering systems, which have significant utility to users.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset relies on Wikipedia, which may have biases. The questions are derived from Google search queries, which may reflect user biases. The dataset focuses on factual questions and may not represent all types of queries (e.g., 'how to' questions were largely excluded).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset focuses on longer queries (8+ words) and excludes 'how to' questions. It is limited to Wikipedia as the source of evidence. The task involves inherent ambiguity in what constitutes a correct answer, leading to variability in annotations. Systems currently perform significantly below human upper bounds.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. The dataset is intended as a benchmark for evaluating question answering systems and driving research in natural language understanding.
